title: When does grievous hurt legally turn into attempt to murder
p1:
A serious injury does not automatically mean it was an attempt to murder.

The surprising part? A person can cause grievous hurt and still not be guilty of attempt to murder if the intention behind the act does not match the legal standard.
p2:
Many people think the severity of the injury alone decides the charge. But the law looks deeper — especially at the intention, the method used, the part of the body targeted, and the circumstances of the attack.

For example, a dangerous attack aimed at a vital body part with the intention of causing death may move from grievous hurt to attempt to murder.
p3:
The key difference is not just 'how badly someone was injured' but 'what the accused was trying to do.' A deep injury caused during a sudden fight may be viewed differently from a planned attack with a deadly weapon.

A useful takeaway: criminal liability often depends on the mindset behind the act, not only the final result.
conclusion: Do you think the intention behind an attack should matter more than the seriousness of the injury when deciding an attempt to murder charge?
